The *Pesalātherīapadāna* (Thi Ap 40) is a verse text belonging to the *Therīapadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya in the Pali Tipiṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. It preserves the biographical and karmic narrative (*apadāna*) of the elder nun Pesalā. SuttaCentral provides no English title for the text, though it records translations in five modern languages [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels are registered for this text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus, the poem shows 254 matching passages across 50 Pali texts, with the heaviest concentration occurring in the commentary to the *Therīgāthā* (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, 61 matches, including §9.3–14.2) and both volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring stock verses and narrative sequences are shared with multiple other apadāna texts, including the *Kuṇḍalakesātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 21), *Lakuṇḍabhaddiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 543), *Khemātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 18), and *Sumedhātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 1) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (e.g. §10.3–10.4), though this correspondence is an automated textual match rather than an established historical parallel [DharmaNexus].
